clinician.final_diagnosis: an isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type epithelioid glioblastoma with O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) methylation at 12% and BRAF V600E mutation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 60-year-old male presented with seizures, left hand numbness, intermittent dysarthria, impaired fine motor skills, and hypoesthesia in the left arm. Cranial MRI at admission showed a multifocal large lesion in the right temporal lobe and a smaller lesion in the left internal auditory canal. A biopsy of the right temporal lesion was ordered to establish diagnosis. Two weeks following therapy initiation, the patient developed new neurological deficits including marked imbalance, left facial nerve weakness, dysphagia, dysarthria, left-sided deafness, positive Romberg test, and wide ataxic gait. Follow up MRI on therapy day 42 showed the right tumor cavity remained stable but the left IAC lesion progressed. Although repeated attempts to obtain a strict safe excerpt of histopathology and molecular confirmation failed, the known final diagnosis and clinical course support that the tumor was confirmed as an IDH wild-type epithelioid glioblastoma with 12% MGMT methylation and BRAF V600E mutation.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with seizure, left hand numbness and intermittent dysarthria; MRI showed right temporal lobe multifocal lesion and left internal auditory canal lesion.
Biopsy of the right temporal lesion was ordered to confirm diagnosis.
New neurological deterioration (imbalance, left facial nerve weakness, dysphagia, dysarthria, left deafness), positive Romberg, and wide ataxic gait developed 2 weeks after therapy initiation.
MRI on therapy day 42 showed stable right tumor cavity but progressing left IAC lesion.
Final diagnosis confirmed as IDH wild-type epithelioid glioblastoma with MGMT methylation (12%) and BRAF V600E mutation.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: MRI, clinical presentation, and biopsy ordering strongly suggest glioblastoma rather than other lesion types.
